conviction_note: Three negative legs (a record Q4 arithmetically embedded in the FY82-83k guide and in FY consensus, a two-quarter pattern of landing at or below the bottom of its own guided ranges, and a Q4 order quarter that opened with the MBA contract rate at 6.97% after a fifth straight monthly fall in new-home applications) sum to about -4.5, against a +1.5 offset from a crowded short base at a 52-week low with a call-rich skew and an industry gross-margin cycle that is visibly inflecting up; net -3.0, i.e. inside the -4.0/-5.2 cluster of the last six prints and well inside the 6.33% implied move, which itself is inflated by the FOMC and August housing starts sitting in the same option.

findings.finding: Lennar's own full-year target of 'approximately 82,000 to 83,000 homes' arithmetically requires a Q4 of 23,118-25,118 deliveries (Q1 16,863 + Q2 20,519 = 37,382; Q3 guided 20,500-21,500), i.e. +0.4% to +9.0% against the 23,034 of Q4 FY25 which was itself the largest delivery quarter in company history, at a moment when new orders are guided down 4-9% year over year against the 23,004 comp.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell side has taken the guide at face value rather than discounting it: FY2026 consensus revenue is $32.47bn (19 analysts, S&P Global, pulled 2026-09-16), only -5.0% on a fiscal 2025 that delivered 82,583 homes, and Q3 consensus revenue of $8.33bn sits exactly on the guide midpoint (Zacks' own model is 21,181 units at $377,230). If a Q4 cut were priced, FY26 consensus revenue would already sit a percent or two below the company's number, the average price target would not be $84.92 (+6% to spot), and the 25-delta skew would be put-bid rather than -0.77. Lennar has already walked this number from 'approximately 85,000' (2025-12-16) to 82,000-83,000 (2026-06-11) without consensus moving below it.
findings.independence: FY26 consensus revenue $32.47bn and PT $84.92 from a different source, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/len/forecast/ (dated 2026-09-16 on page); Q4 FY25 actual of 23,034 deliveries and FY25 total of 82,583 from a third, https://newsroom.lennar.com/2025-12-16-Lennar-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2025-Results (2025-12-16). NOTE: this finding and finding 2 both draw on the 2026-06-11 release, but on different lines of it (the FY delivery target vs the Q3 margin guide) and each rests principally on a different primary document.

findings.finding: Lennar has printed at or below the bottom of its own guided ranges for two consecutive quarters: Q1 FY26 delivered 16,863 homes against a guide of 17,000-18,000 (below the range entirely) with gross margin 15.2% against a guided 15.0-16.0%, and Q2 FY26 gross margin was 15.6% against a guided 15.5-16.0% — so the Q3 guide of 'approximately 16%' more plausibly prints 15.5-15.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes a builder's guide-to-actual hit rate, and consensus is modelling the midpoint, not the floor: Zacks' Q3 model is 21,181 deliveries at $377,230 ASP — dead centre of the guided bands — and the consensus EPS has drifted only from $1.31 to $1.29 in the past week. If the market had priced the pattern, consensus would sit a nickel or more below the guide-midpoint arithmetic rather than on it. On roughly 21,000 homes at ~$377k, each 30bp of gross margin is about $24m pre-tax, near $0.07 a share, or 5% of the $1.29 consensus per 30bp.
findings.independence: The Q1 FY26 guide (17,000-18,000 deliveries, 15.0-16.0% margin) comes from a separate primary document, https://newsroom.lennar.com/2025-12-16-Lennar-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2025-Results (2025-12-16), while the Q1 actual and Q2 guide come from the 2026-03-12 release and the Q2 actual from the 2026-06-11 8-K; consensus sitting at the guide midpoint is independently confirmed at https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/heres-investors-must-know-ahead-133600368.html (2026-09-15).

findings.finding: Lennar's Q4 order quarter (September-November) opened with the MBA 30-year fixed contract rate at 6.97% for the week ending 2026-09-11, up 12bp week over week, after the MBA Builder Application Survey showed new-home purchase applications fell 6% month over month and 5.5% year over year in August — a fifth consecutive monthly decline, with MBA's implied new-home sales pace 9% below a year ago and the average new-home loan size down to $373,194 from $374,438.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate level is macro and is in the tape (LEN is -5.9% over 20 days and 2.6% off its 52-week low), but the specific company-level contradiction is not: Lennar guided Q3 ASP UP sequentially to $375,000-$380,000 from an actual $371,000 in Q2, while the industry's average new-home loan size fell in both July and August. That is the one line in tonight's table with an independent third-party dataset pointing the other way, and it is the line that drives the revenue print. If it were priced, Q3 consensus revenue of $8.33bn would not be modelled on a $377,230 ASP.
findings.independence: Freddie Mac's separate PMMS survey shows three consecutive weekly increases into mid-September (6.66% to 6.71% to 6.76%), https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/10/3359803/0/en/mortgage-rates-average-6-76.html (2026-09-10, confirmed in the URL path); and Millrose Properties' CEO — Lennar's own land banker, 68% of whose invested capital is the Lennar Master Program Agreement — said on 2026-08-11 that it is 'unquestionably a tough market, particularly at the first time buyer segment' with 'full year 2026 delivery guidance moving lower across the largest public builders', https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/millrose-properties-mrp-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

findings.finding: The offsetting leg: roughly 8.5% of LEN's free float is short and up about 4.5% over the past month on a cheap 0.37% borrow, the stock sits 2.6% off a 52-week low and 40% off its high, the 25-delta skew is -0.77 (calls richer than puts), and the industry gross-margin cycle is visibly inflecting up — Hovnanian's May-July quarter reported homebuilding gross margin of 14.6% before interest and land charges, improving sequentially for a second consecutive quarter, the same shape as Lennar's own 15.2% to 15.6% to ~16% sequence.
findings.why_not_priced: Six of the last seven LEN prints fell and they clustered tightly between -4.0% and -5.2%, which is the reaction function the market is carrying into tonight; what that reaction function does not contain is that this is the first of those prints where the company's own margin sequence is rising rather than falling and where a peer on a later calendar has independently confirmed a second consecutive quarter of sequential margin recovery. If the market had priced the downside as hard as the history implies, the 25-delta skew would be positive and put-bid rather than -0.77 with a 0.89 put/call open-interest ratio. This caps the realised downside well short of the -4.5% historical mean.
findings.independence: The margin-inflection half rests on a completely separate company's primary release, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/20/3348449/12793/en/hovnanian-enterprises-reports-fiscal-2026-third-quarter-results.html (2026-08-20, confirmed in the URL path), and the skew and 52-week-low figures come from the sealed baseline rather than from Ortex.

A revenue-consensus-vs-guidance gap: I initially computed consensus revenue as sitting above the guide-implied number and it does not — $8.33bn reconciles to 21,181 deliveries at $377,230 plus non-homebuilding revenue, i.e. the guide midpoint. Dropped.
baseline_tension: My negative legs agree with the run-up (-5.9% over 20 days, 2.6% off the 52-week low) and with the six-of-seven negative reaction history, which is precisely why I have sized them well below that history's -4.5% mean; my one positive leg cuts against that history and agrees with the skew, which at -0.77 says the option market is not paying for downside here — and note the 6.33% 'event implied move' is overstated as an earnings anchor because the 2026-09-18 straddle it was struck from also spans today's 2pm FOMC decision and dot plot and the 08:30 ET August housing starts release on 09-17.
